questions.question: The average of three numbers is 23. If two numbers are 11 and 25, the third number is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of three numbers = 23

Two numbers are 11 and 25

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all numbers) / (Total count of numbers)

**Calculation:**

Average = (Number 1 + Number 2 + Number 3) / 3

Sum of all numbers = Average × Total count

Sum of all numbers = 23 × 3

⇒ Sum of all numbers = 69

Number 3 = Sum of all numbers - (Number 1 + Number 2)

⇒ Number 3 = 69 - (11 + 25)

⇒ Number 3 = 69 - 36

⇒ Number 3 = 33

**The third number is 33.**

questions.question: Akshay has ₹1,218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Arjun and Kartik and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. It was seen that Arjun and Kartik got the same amount after 12 and 13 years, respectively. How much amount (in ₹) did Akshay give to Kartik?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The total amount Akshay has = ₹1,218.

Both Arjun and Kartik invest the amount at 10% interest per annum, compounded annually.

Arjun invests for 12 years, and Kartik invests for 13 years, and they receive the same amount after the respective time periods.

**Formula used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + r / 100)t

Where:

P = Principal amount, r = rate of interest, t = time period, A = amount after interest

**Calculations:**

Let the amount given to Arjun be P₁ and the amount given to Kartik be P₂.

Since the total amount is ₹1,218, we have:

P₁ + P₂ = 1,218

The amount received by both after the respective years is the same, so we have:

P₁ × (1 + 10 / 100)¹² = P₂ × (1 + 10 / 100)¹³

⇒ P₁ × (1.1)¹² = P₂ × (1.1)¹³

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (1.1)¹³ / (1.1)¹²

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = 1.1

⇒ P₁ = 1.1 × P₂

Now, substitute P₁ = 1.1 × P₂ into the total amount equation:

1.1 × P₂ + P₂ = 1,218

⇒ 2.1 × P₂ = 1,218

⇒ P₂ = 1,218 ÷ 2.1 = 580

**∴ Akshay gave ₹580 to Kartik.**

questions.question:
The mean and the mode of a set of data are 47.4 and 61.6, respectively. Find the median of the data set, using the empirical formula.

(Round off your answer to one decimal place.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mean of the data set = 47.4

Mode of the data set = 61.6

**Formula Used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

**Calculation:**

Using the formula:

Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean)

⇒ 61.6 = 3(Median) - 2(47.4)

⇒ 61.6 = 3(Median) - 94.8

⇒ 3(Median) = 61.6 + 94.8

⇒ 3(Median) = 156.4

⇒ Median = 156.4 / 3

⇒ Median = 52.1

**The median of the data set is 52.1 (correct option: 1).**

questions.question: If 1 is added to each odd digit and 2 is subtracted from each even digit in the number 3816427, how many digits will appear more than once in the new number thus formed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number is 3816427. We need to add 1 to each odd digit and subtract 2 from each even digit.

**Calculations:**

Let's break down the number and apply the changes:

Digit 3 (odd) → 3 + 1 = 4

Digit 8 (even) → 8 - 2 = 6

Digit 1 (odd) → 1 + 1 = 2

Digit 6 (even) → 6 - 2 = 4

Digit 4 (even) → 4 - 2 = 2

Digit 2 (even) → 2 - 2 = 0

Digit 7 (odd) → 7 + 1 = 8

So, the new number formed is 4624028.

Now, let's identify the digits that appear more than once:

The digits in 4624028 are 4, 6, 2, 4, 0, 2, 8. We can see that the digits 4, 2 appear more than once.

Two digits (4 and 2) appear more than once in the new number.

**∴ The number of digits that appear more than once is 2.**

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(7) of his normal speed, Manish is 20 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance be t minutes.

Manish walks at 5/7 of his normal speed and is 20 minutes late.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Difference in time = Normal time - Late time

**Calculations:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time be t.

Distance = Speed × Time = S × t

When walking at 5/7 of his normal speed, the speed becomes (5/7) × S.

The time taken to cover the same distance at this speed is:

New time = (S × t) ÷ (5/7 × S) = (7 × t) ÷ 5

So, the difference in time is:

Difference = New time - Normal time = (7 × t) ÷ 5 - t

Given, the difference in time is 20 minutes:

(7t ÷ 5) - t = 20

⇒ (7t ÷ 5) - (5t ÷ 5) = 20

⇒ 2t ÷ 5 = 20

⇒ t = 20 × 5 / 2 = 50 minutes

**∴ The usual time taken by Manish to cover the distance is 50 minutes.**

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cone is 1078 cm³. Find the total surface area of the cone if its height is 21 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Volume of a cone = 1078 cm³

Height of the cone = 21 cm

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone, V = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Slant height, l = √(r² + h²)

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a cone = π × r × (r + l)

**Calculation:**

From the volume formula:

Volume, V = (1/3) × π × r² × h

⇒ 1078 = (1/3) × (22/7) × r² × 21

⇒ 1078 = (22/7) × r² × 7

⇒ 1078 = 22 × r²

⇒ r² = 1078 / 22

⇒ r² = 49

⇒ r = √49

⇒ r = 7 cm

Now, calculate the slant height (l):

l = √(r² + h²)

⇒ l = √(7² + 21²)

⇒ l = √(49 + 441)

⇒ l = √490

⇒ l = 7√10

Now, calculate the Total Surface Area (TSA):

TSA = π × r × (r + l)

⇒ TSA = (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 7√10)

⇒ TSA = 22 × (7 + 7√10)

⇒ TSA = 154 × (1 + √10) cm²

The Total Surface Area of the cone is 154(1 + √10) cm².

questions.question: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 960. If the smaller of these two integers is represented by x, which of the options below will correspond to the equation for finding the value of x?

Rearrange the equation:

questions.question: A can finish a work in 2 days and B can do the same work in 52 days. B worked alone for 26 days and left the job. In how many days can A alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish a work in 2 days.

B can finish the same work in 52 days.

B worked alone for 26 days and left the job.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Rate × Time

LCM method for combined work calculation.

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/2

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/52

LCM of 2 and 52 = 52

Total work = 52 units (assuming the work as a whole unit divided into 52 equal parts).

Work done by B in 26 days = 26 × (1/52)

Work done by B in 26 days = 26/52

Work done by B in 26 days = 1/2

Remaining work = Total work - Work done by B

Remaining work = 1 - 1/2

Remaining work = 1/2

A's efficiency = 1/2 work per day.

Days required by A to finish remaining work:

⇒ Remaining work / A's efficiency

⇒ (1/2) / (1/2)

⇒ 1 day

**A alone can finish the remaining work in 1 day.**

2. Marked Price (MP) = SP / (1 - Discount%).

3. Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Gain%).

**Calculation:**

Discount = 80% = 0.80.

Marked Price ⇒ MP = SP / (1 - Discount%).

MP = 5180 / (1 - 0.80).

MP = 5180 / 0.20.

MP = ₹25,900.

Cost Price ⇒ CP = SP / (1 + Gain%).

CP = 25,900 / (1 + 0.48).

CP = 25,900 / 1.48.

CP ⇒ ₹17,500.

**The cost price of the oven is ₹17,500.**

questions.solution:

Selling price (SP) when there is a 5% loss = ₹950

Loss percentage = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 - Loss%)

Gain percentage (x%) = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

**Calculation:**

Loss% = 5% = 5/100 = 0.05

CP = SP / (1 - Loss%)

⇒ CP = 950 / (1 - 0.05)

⇒ CP = 950 / 0.95

⇒ CP = ₹1,000

Calculate the gain percentage (x%) for SP = ₹1,360:

Gain% = [(SP - CP) / CP] × 100

⇒ Gain% = [(1,360 - 1,000) / 1,000] × 100

⇒ Gain% = [360 / 1,000] × 100

⇒ Gain% = 36%

**The value of x is 36%, and the correct option is Option 1.**

questions.question: C is the third proportional of 29 and B. If B is the sum of the first three even natural numbers, then find the value of C. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

B is the sum of the first three even natural numbers.

C is the third proportional of 29 and B.

**Formula Used:**

C = (B²) / A

**Calculation:**

First three even natural numbers = 2, 4, and 6.

Sum of the first three even natural numbers (B) = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12

Given A = 29 and B = 12, we use the formula:

C = (B²) / A

⇒ C = (12²) / 29

⇒ C = 144 / 29

⇒ C ≈ 4.97

**The value of C is approximately 4.97.**

questions.question: Two positive numbers differ by 2858. When the greater number is divided by the smaller number, the quotient is 5 and the remainder is 178. What is the HCF of the greater of the two given numbers and 3828?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Let the two positive numbers be x (greater number) and y (smaller number).

The difference between the two numbers is 2858, so:

x - y = 2858

When the greater number is divided by the smaller number, the quotient is 5, and the remainder is 178. So:

x = 5y + 178

Calculations:

We have two equations:

1. x - y = 2858

2. x = 5y + 178

Substitute the value of x from equation (2) into equation (1):

(5y + 178) - y = 2858

⇒ 5y - y + 178 = 2858

⇒ 4y + 178 = 2858

⇒ 4y = 2858 - 178

⇒ 4y = 2680

⇒ y = 2680 ÷ 4 = 670

Now, substitute the value of y into equation (2) to find x:

x = 5 × 670 + 178

⇒ x = 3350 + 178 = 3528

The two numbers are 3528 (greater number) and 670 (smaller number).

Now, we need to find the HCF of the greater number (3528) and 3828.

**Using the Euclidean algorithm:**

We find the HCF of 3528 and 3828 by subtracting the smaller number from the larger number:

3828 - 3528 = 300

Now, find the HCF of 3528 and 300:

3528 ÷ 300 = 11 remainder 228

300 ÷ 228 = 1 remainder 72

228 ÷ 72 = 3 remainder 12

72 ÷ 12 = 6 remainder 0

Thus, the HCF of 3528 and 3828 is 12.

**∴ The HCF of the greater of the two given numbers (3528) and 3828 is 12.**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 84 minutes and 36 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 42 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 84 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 36 minutes

Both pipes are opened together, and the cistern should be completely filled in 42 minutes. We need to find the time after which Pipe B should be turned off.

**Formula used:**

Efficiency of a pipe = 1 / Time taken to fill the cistern

Work done by a pipe in 1 minute = Efficiency of the pipe

**Calculations:**

Efficiency of Pipe A = 1 / 84 (portion of the cistern filled by Pipe A in 1 minute)

Efficiency of Pipe B = 1 / 36 (portion of the cistern filled by Pipe B in 1 minute)

Let Pipe B be turned off after t minutes. In the first t minutes, both pipes A and B work together, and in the remaining (42 - t) minutes, only Pipe A works.

The total work done by both pipes is 1 (to completely fill the cistern), so we can write the equation:

Work done by Pipe A in 42 minutes + Work done by Pipe B in t minutes = 1

Work done by Pipe A in 42 minutes = 42 × (1 / 84) = 1/2

Work done by Pipe B in t minutes = t × (1 / 36) = t / 36

Now, set up the equation for total work done:

(1/2) + (t / 36) = 1

⇒ t / 36 = 1 - 1/2

⇒ t / 36 = 1/2

⇒ t = (1/2) × 36 = 18

**∴ Pipe B should be turned off after 18 minutes.**

questions.question: The average of Anwar's marks in seven subjects is 75. His average in six subjects excluding Science is 70. How many marks did he get in Science?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of Anwar's marks in 7 subjects = 75.

Average of his marks in 6 subjects excluding Science = 70.

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of items

Marks in Science = Total marks in 7 subjects - Total marks in 6 subjects excluding Science

**Calculation:**

Total marks in 7 subjects = 75 × 7

⇒ Total marks in 7 subjects = 525

Total marks in 6 subjects excluding Science = 70 × 6

⇒ Total marks in 6 subjects excluding Science = 420

Marks in Science = 525 - 420

⇒ Marks in Science = 105

**The marks obtained by Anwar in Science are 105.**

questions.question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 21 g/cm³. Its internal and external radii are 8 cm and 9 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in kg) of the shell?

( {Use} pi = (22)/(7), {Density} = frac{{Mass}}{{Volume}} )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Density of the metal = 21 g/cm³

Internal radius of the hollow shell (r₁) = 8 cm

External radius of the hollow shell (r₂) = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

Density = Mass / Volume

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × r³

Weight = Mass × g (where g = acceleration due to gravity = 9.8 m/s²)

**Calculation:**

Volume of the metal shell = Volume of external sphere - Volume of internal sphere

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × (9)3 - (4/3) × (22/7) × (8)3

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × [729 - 512]

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22/7) × 217

Volume of the metal shell = (4/3) × (22) × 31

Volume of the metal shell = 909.33

Mass of the shell = Density × Volume

⇒ Mass = 21 × 909.33

⇒ Mass = 19095.93 g

Convert mass to kg:

⇒ Mass = 19095.93 / 1000

⇒ Mass ≈ 19.096 kg

**The weight of the hollow spherical shell is approximately 19.096**** kg.**

⇒ 20x = 360°

⇒ x = 18°

Now, the angles are:

∠P = 2x = 36°, ∠Q = 8x = 144°, ∠R = 3x = 54°, ∠S = 7x = 126°.

Since the sum of opposite angles is not equal, the quadrilateral is a trapezium.
